source.title: A Deeper Analysis of Block-Sparse Featurizers

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent garbling or cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the geometry and recovery of sparse features using block-sparse featurizers on synthetic manifolds, a different method and setting from the original toy-model superposition work. It also tests how block splitting changes with sparsity and architecture.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates BSF and SAE recovery of synthetic concept manifolds and reports block splitting, seed variation, and sparsity-sweep outcomes. These bear on the geometric and sparsity-related parts of V1 and on V6. It does not test feature importance or a classic overcomplete toy network with more features than dimensions. The brief DINOv3/CLIP experiments are vision-model results, not LLM results. Hyperparameter values used to select settings are not recorded as outcomes unless the text reports an outcome for them.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper about block-sparse featurizers (BSFs). The manifold features in its synthetic 'Manifold Zoo' are planted by design: 128 features, each embedded through a random orthonormal frame. No network learns these representations. All results measure how well BSF and SAE variants recover the planted features. So they test the featurizer, not whether models store features in superposition (V1), whether model features are 1-D (V6), or whether SAE features are the model's units (V5). The BSF/SAE comparisons pit the study's own method against baselines. The DINOv3/CLIP section is brief, gives no numbers, and concerns featurizer behaviour (blocks split features). It is not a measurement of superposition or of feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say the BSF recovers manifold features as single units where SAEs tile them. Features still split across blocks, as near-orthogonal complements, even without data correlations; Tournament Top-K recovers much of this. Mixed block dimensions fail because features lock into wrong-sized blocks early in training. Block crosscoders have a merging problem that dedicated feature columns partly fix.
record.recipe_differences: Uses top-k Grassmannian block-sparse featurizers with orthonormal frames on synthetic manifold data and brief vision-model experiments; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature splitting persists across G = 128, 256, and 512; increasing top-k from 4 to 6 to 8 degrades performance, with no single-block feature recovery at k = 8. The 10-seed results vary by feature type. Correlated and independent datasets give similar BSF seed results, while SAE and post-hoc SAE recovery differ across those datasets. Mixed block-size outcomes depend on the selection regime.

fits_no_version.finding: On planted synthetic manifolds, the BSF splits about some features across two near-orthogonal blocks. This persists across G and worsens with k. SAEs tile the manifolds (raw-atom R2 0.36 vs BSF 0.77).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Block/subspace featurizers still split multi-dimensional features across units, as SAEs do.

fits_no_version.finding: Tournament Top-K raises the fraction of well-recovered manifolds from 0.77 to 0.90. Featurizers with mixed block dimensions fail to sort features by dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Featurizer design choices determine how planted manifold features are recovered.

record.problems: The central controlled evidence is synthetic. The real-model section is explicitly brief and reports no exact causal-ablation values or model-separated results. The text gives no error bars, confidence intervals, or p-values for the reported recovery outcomes. The authors state they do not fully understand why splits form.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted under the 60-row limit. The paper also mentions cross-model matching, artificial rendered features, layer-to-layer maps, and block-crosscoder experiments; these were not included because the reported outcomes do not directly test the versions selected here, or concern a different crosscoder-specific merging problem.

untested.parts: No network is trained on sparse features to see how it stores them. Sparsity transition, geometry and importance are not examined in a model.
SAE stability, completeness and canonicity in real models are not tested. The SAE results are only recovery of planted synthetic manifolds.
Multi-dimensional features are assumed as the data-generating process, not measured in a model.

record.verdict_notes: The reader treated featurizer recovery of planted manifolds as evidence on V1 and V6. But the manifold geometry is imposed by the data generator, so recovery results test the featurizer, not the claim. I removed the record's labels for that reason. The vision-model experiments give no quantitative results.

versions.untested_parts: Tests sparse synthetic manifold features and block geometry, including the effects of block sparsity and block count. Does not test the classic toy-network regime of more features than dimensions, importance-dependent allocation, or the original toy-model intervention and measure.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity pressure or whether important features obtain dedicated dimensions.
Does not test polysemantic neurons or whether they arise without capacity pressure.
The real-model experiments are on DINOv3 and CLIP, not LLMs; they do not test the stated LLM evidence claim.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units. Its seed-stability and splitting results concern BSFs, not SAE features.

Tests multidimensional manifold features and block/subspace representations, mainly in synthetic data. Does not test whether superposition in the original toy networks consists of one-dimensional directions or whether this holds across LLMs.

rows.subject: Manifold Zoo (synthetic)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked subspace overlap for pairs of blocks that split a feature during BSF training
rows.measure: Geometric overlap between the two block subspaces
rows.baseline: random-pair overlap; split-pair overlap initially described as 2x the random baseline
rows.value: The blocks end up as almost orthogonal components of the same feature; initial overlap is approximately 0.3.
rows.note: The paper proposes an explanation for the development of near-orthogonal complementary blocks, while noting that the phenomenon is not fully understood.
rows.check: Training dynamics of split BSF block pairs. The near-orthogonality is between featurizer blocks, not model feature directions. The ~0.3 overlap is a mid-training value, not the initial one.

source_check.correct: Across 83 split block pairs, specialization starts around epoch 3. Subspace overlap subsequently grows to approximately 0.3, twice the random baseline, before declining toward near-orthogonality. Initial overlap is not numerically stated.

relation.reason: Sparse feature decomposition motivates and underlies the method, but its results do not establish superposition, feature dimensionality, or canonical SAE units in the systems named by the claim versions.

tranche.reason: The study assumes sparse manifold representations and evaluates featurizer recovery and architectural changes. Synthetic features are planted; the brief vision experiments report tool performance without testing a claim version.

source_check.notes: The rows report featurizer performance and diagnostics, not claim-effect evidence; their none links and cannot_determine states are appropriate. In r14, 0.77 and 0.90 are fractions of well-recovered manifolds, distinct from Table 1's mean recovery R2.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic Manifold Zoo, especially the block-count and top-k sweeps
reader_labels.reason: The study finds persistent feature splitting even when G = M, and increasing k worsens recovery, with no feature captured by one block at k = 8; this qualifies any simple one-feature/one-direction geometric account (r11–r12).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The split blocks become almost orthogonal components of the same feature, consistent with a near-orthogonal decomposition, although this is a block-subspace result rather than the classic toy-network direction result (r13).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic features with manifold geometry and mixed block dimensions
reader_labels.reason: The study represents curved and other manifold features using multi-dimensional blocks and reports dimension-dependent assignment failures, rather than finding that all features are one-dimensional directions (r9, r15–r18).
